title: A monotone version the rank-aware join can read, stable under replay
description: versionRank already ranks by a `version` number before falling back to updatedAt and canonical JSON. Give SprintContract that field and write it at sprint_exit — replay-stably, because a fixed clock makes updatedAt useless as a tiebreak and a wall-clock-derived version would make every golden case irreproducible.

successCriteria.description: SprintContractSchema declares version?: number, optional so all 250 committed contracts stay valid without migration.
sprint_exit writes a monotone version on the settled contract.
The written version is REPLAY-STABLE: two runs over the same input produce the same value, and a captured golden case replays byte-identically. Proven by execution, not argument.

A test asserts the settled copy outranks the seeded one under versionRank AND that the ordering does not depend on updatedAt — construct both copies with an identical updatedAt, as the fixed clock produces, and confirm the version still decides.

A round-trip test proves the version survives saveContract followed by loadContract. This is the asymmetry that ruled out riding as an unknown key: loadContract parses through a non-strict schema that strips them.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green; golden gate still passes.

nonGoals: Changing mergeEntries — that is sprint 4. This sprint only supplies the field it will read.
Deriving the version from wall-clock time, run order, or anything else a replay cannot reproduce.
stopConditions: No replay-stable monotone source is available at sprint_exit — stop and report what is, rather than shipping something a replay cannot reproduce.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: versionRank is at src/pge/registry/reducers.ts:348-359 and reads value.version (finite number) then value.updatedAt then canonicalJson. You are supplying the first. The replay-stability constraint is the hard part: the golden harness runs on a fixed clock, so anything time-derived collapses. Look at what sprint_exit already has in hand that is monotone and reproducible — attempt counts and branch status are candidates; verify whichever you choose actually increases across the seeded-to-settled transition. sc-3-4 is the criterion that proves you did not accidentally rely on updatedAt.
evaluatorNotes: sc-3-3 is the one to hammer. Run the same input twice and diff the version. Then capture and replay a golden case and confirm byte-identical. If the generator derived the version from anything time-like or order-like, this is where it shows. For sc-3-4, build both copies with the SAME updatedAt yourself and confirm the ordering still holds — a test that passes only because updatedAt happened to differ proves nothing.
